number_of_offences: Allegations under Sections 166, 167, 418, 420, 465, 468, 471, 409, 209 and 109 read with Sections 120-B, 34 and 37 of the Indian Penal Code, and Sections 12 and 13(2) read with Sections 13(1)(c) and (d) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988. The number of offences finally upheld is not stated.
financial_property_loss: Rs. 370 crores siphoned off from the government funds of the APSSDC
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the evidence that the appellant was implicated for the other offences under IPC and that the Special Court had the jurisdiction to pass the remand order.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses by noting that the investigating agency had the right to investigate the crime which took place prior to the amended provision of Section 13, and that the deletion of the said provisions and substitution of the new offence under Section 13 by the Amendment Act, 2018 would not affect the right of the investigating agency to investigate.

investigation_status: FIR registered in 2021, accused added on 08.09.2021, remand order passed on 10.09.2023
procedural_irregularity: Absence of prior approval under s.17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the appellant was the mastermind behind the diversion of public funds, having unilaterally appointed officials and approved the cost estimation with criminal intent. The State also contended that the FIR and remand order were valid and that the Special Court had jurisdiction to proceed against the appellant for the alleged offences under the IPC and the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the initiation of proceedings against the appellant was invalid due to non-compliance with Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, which requires prior approval from the appropriate authority for any enquiry, inquiry, or investigation into offences committed by a public servant. They also contended that the entire proceeding would collapse if the allegations under the 1988 Act were found to be invalid.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the legislative intent of the Prevention of Corruption (Amendment) Act, 2018 was to make Section 17A applicable only to new offences and not to those existing prior to the amendment. The Court also emphasized that the right of the investigating agency to investigate offences committed before the amendment is not affected by the repeal of the old provisions.
